newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: LESS JAPANESE TOURISTS COMING TO AUSTRALIA
The Chairman of the Australian Tourist Commission says Japanese tourists are now more price conscious travellers, leading to a decline in the number coming to Australia.
That's despite an overall increase in Japanese travelling overseas.
Don Morris says Australia is an expensive destination for the Japanese, largely because of air fares.
Mr Morris says there's about a 30 per cent difference on the current package deals available to Hawaii, as compared to the Gold Coast.
NSW STATE MP LOSES BATTLE OVER PAEDOPHILES INQUIRY

New South Wales state government backbencher, Franca Arena, has lost out in her campaign for greater powers for the Police Royal Commission, to pursue paedophiles. An amendment put by Ms Arena has failed to win support in a special meeting of Caucus, with members instead voting in favour of the new terms of reference put by the Premier yesterday.
ABORIGINAL AND TORRES STRAIT ISLANDER DEATH RATES FALLING
Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander death rates are falling, but not as fast as in the Australian population as a whole.
The Institute of Health and Welfare has found that in the decade to 1994, there was very little improvement in the mortality of indigenous people.
Death rates have dropped slightly for indigenous men, but there's been no corresponding decline for indigenous women.
The report says the overall decline in mortality did not significantly reduce the gap between indigenous and non-indigenous death rates.
Cardiovascular disease remains the main cause of death and more than three times higher than the rate in non-indigenous Australians.
Indigenous death rates were higher than expected for every cause of death examined, except for breast cancer and suicide in women, and prostate cancer for men.
BORBIDGE SAYS HANSON COULD HIT TRADE
Queensland's Premier says comments about Asian immigration by Independent Federal MP, Pauline Hanson, may hit the state's trade with the region.
Rob Borbidge, who's just back from a trip to China, says Ms Hanson's comments weren't raised with him by Chinese officials.
But Borbidge says a number of Australian business-people in Asia are concerned about the impact they could have.
He says Asia buys much of what Queensland produces and exports and that comments deemed insulting by Asian people may lead to a loss of jobs in Queensland.
